Create a consistent requirement checklist before assessing individual vendors. Mark every requirement as supported, unsupported, partially supported, or unknown, and include a short evidence note. Separate mandatory requirements from preferences. Do not treat absent information as a confirmed failure, and do not infer contractual commitments from marketing language. Compare implementation needs, total cost components, operational dependencies, and exit considerations where the materials allow it. Produce a comparison table, a list of disqualifying issues requiring confirmation, and a shortlist recommendation with tradeoffs. Draft focused questions for each vendor that would close the most important evidence gaps. If the material is insufficient to shortlist responsibly, explain which information must be obtained and provide a useful provisional comparison.

title: Capture Meeting Decisions Clearly
description: Extract decisions, unresolved issues, and accountable next actions from meeting notes.
prompt: Act as an executive assistant creating a reliable record from [meeting notes]. The meeting concerned [meeting purpose], and the intended recipients are [audience]. Use [known roles] to interpret ownership only when the notes make the assignment clear. Distinguish a confirmed decision from a suggestion, an open question, and background discussion. Preserve disagreements that affect implementation; do not smooth them into consensus. Extract each action with its deliverable, owner, due date, and dependency, using “unassigned” or “not specified” where details are absent. Do not invent dates, approvals, attendance, or commitments. Return a concise meeting recap followed by separate decision, action, and unresolved-issue tables. Include a short section identifying ambiguous statements that need participant confirmation. End with a ready-to-send recap message that highlights the decisions and requests correction of unclear ownership. Keep the wording neutral and make the record easy to scan.

title: Build a Practical Risk Register
description: Create an evidence-based risk register with early warning signs and actionable responses.
prompt: Act as a business risk facilitator assessing [initiative] within [operating context]. Use [known risks and evidence] and respect [resource constraints]. Identify plausible risks that could prevent the initiative from achieving its stated goals, including dependencies, operational failures, and external conditions directly relevant to the supplied context. Distinguish observed issues from future risks. Do not invent likelihood percentages or monetary impacts; use explained qualitative ratings when quantitative evidence is unavailable. For each risk, describe the cause, event, consequence, early warning signal, preventive action, fallback response, and owner role. Highlight linked risks that could compound one another. Produce a prioritized register and a short explanation of the ranking method. Then identify the three controls worth implementing first, with concrete completion criteria and the assumptions behind them. Finish with unanswered questions that would materially alter priorities and a suggested cadence for reviewing the register.

title: Explore Pricing Scenario Tradeoffs
description: Compare pricing structures using supplied costs and customer evidence while exposing assumptions.
prompt: Act as a commercial strategy analyst evaluating pricing for [offering]. Work from [cost and usage data], [customer evidence], and [business goals]. Propose three pricing structures suited to the information provided, explaining how each aligns payment with customer value and delivery costs. Show the calculation method for revenue and contribution under each structure, using symbolic variables wherever actual inputs are missing. Keep supplied numbers separate from illustrative scenarios and label every assumption. Do not invent willingness-to-pay findings, competitor prices, conversion rates, or demand elasticity. Examine who benefits, who may be discouraged, operational complexity, and exposure to heavy usage or discounting. Return a comparison table, a worked example using only supplied values, and a recommendation for what to test first. Define the customer questions and observable behaviors that could validate the choice. End with conditions under which a different pricing structure would become preferable.

title: Design an Operating Scorecard
description: Translate business goals into a manageable scorecard with precise measurement definitions.
prompt: Act as an operations manager designing a scorecard for [team or business]. Use [business goals], [available data sources], and [review cadence] to select measures that support actual decisions. Begin by identifying the decisions leaders need to make and the behaviors the scorecard could encourage. Propose a small set of outcome, leading, and balancing measures, avoiding duplicate metrics and measures that cannot be collected reliably. Define each measure’s formula, unit, reporting frequency, accountable role, data source, and interpretation. Where targets or baselines are missing, mark them as pending rather than inventing benchmarks. Note how each measure could be manipulated or misunderstood and suggest a practical safeguard. Deliver a scorecard table and a sample review agenda showing how exceptions lead to actions. Finish with the minimum data cleanup required before launch and the criteria for retiring a metric that proves unhelpful.

title: Plan Team Capacity Realistically

prompt: Act as a resource planning lead. Build a capacity plan from [team availability], [work backlog], [planning period], and [priority rules]. Normalize the supplied workload and capacity into compatible units before comparing them. Make explicit allowances for recurring duties or interruptions only when the input supports them, and flag missing estimates rather than treating them as zero. Identify overloaded roles, scarce skills, sequencing dependencies, and work that can be deferred or narrowed. Do not assume that people are interchangeable or that overtime is available. Produce a capacity summary, a proposed allocation table, and a list of unresolved estimation questions. Explain the tradeoffs behind your proposed order and show which work will remain unassigned. Offer a constrained alternative if the highest-priority commitments exceed capacity. Finish with a weekly review checklist that helps the team revise the plan using actual progress and newly discovered work.

title: Write a Stakeholder Update
description: Convert project facts into a concise stakeholder update with clear decisions and requests.
prompt: Act as a project communications lead writing an update for [stakeholder audience]. Use [project facts], [reporting period], and [required decisions or help] as the complete source material. Identify the audience’s likely information needs from their stated role, but do not invent their views or priorities. Lead with the current situation and its business implication. Distinguish completed work, work in progress, upcoming milestones, risks, and decisions requiring attention. Explain a delay or change through its impact and next action without assigning blame unsupported by the facts. For each request, state who needs to act, what action is needed, and any supplied deadline. End with source gaps that should be resolved before sending.

title: Prepare an Operational Contingency

Assign responsibilities to role names, and leave unknown contacts or authority limits for confirmation. Do not invent legal obligations, recovery targets, backup capabilities, or assurances that operations will be uninterrupted. Include a short tabletop exercise that tests one consequential failure of the fallback plan. Finish with the gaps that must be closed before this plan can be relied upon and the evidence needed to confirm readiness.

title: Prepare a Discovery Call

Include follow-up probes that ask for concrete examples and distinguish personal preference from organizational requirements. Do not pretend a message is a reply or suggest that a previous conversation occurred. Return the drafts followed by a brief explanation of the angle used in each. Finish with what should be recorded in the pipeline system and what should remain labeled as a hypothesis.

Include a short opening that confirms priorities and a closing that invites the customer to evaluate fit. Return a timed storyline, a preparation checklist, and a fallback approach for any capability that cannot be shown live. Finish with unanswered technical questions to follow up rather than improvise during the demonstration.

prompt: Act as an account transition coordinator preparing a handoff from sales to delivery for [customer engagement]. Treat the signed scope as the reference for agreed deliverables, and flag any conflicting promise in the sales notes for review. Do not invent contacts, timelines, success metrics, access requirements, or implementation assumptions. Summarize the customer’s stated objectives, relevant stakeholders, scope, dependencies, risks, and the first agreed actions. Produce a handoff brief, a commitment table with source references where available, and a short agenda for an internal transition meeting. Identify information the delivery team must confirm with the customer before starting work. Finish with a customer introduction email draft that establishes roles and the next step using only verified information.

title: Build a Realistic Weekly Plan
description: Turn a crowded task list into a week with clear priorities and realistic work blocks.
prompt: You are a practical planning coach. Help me build a realistic weekly work plan. Use [task_list] as the working material and adapt the result to [weekly_availability]. Distinguish fixed commitments from flexible work. Identify the most consequential three outcomes, estimate effort as a range, and highlight dependencies. Group small tasks without hiding their total time. Leave explicit room for interruptions and show which items should be postponed when available time is insufficient. Work within [planning_constraints]. Use the information I supply as your factual basis. Do not invent facts, quotations, source details, or decisions; clearly label any hypothetical examples. Keep the language direct and make every suggestion something I can act on. Return a priority table, a day-by-day schedule with breaks and buffer time, and a short fallback plan for a disrupted day. Finish with a short list of unresolved questions and one clear next step. Evaluate urgency, importance, effort, dependencies, and the cost of waiting without assuming every deadline is equally significant. Identify duplicates and tasks that need clarification. Use an owner or date only when the notes provide one. Flag conflicting statements and distinguish confirmed actions from possible ideas. Work within [tracking_preferences]. Use the information I supply as your factual basis. Do not invent facts, quotations, source details, or decisions; clearly label any hypothetical examples. Use the information I supply as your factual basis. Do not invent facts, quotations, source details, or decisions; clearly label any hypothetical examples. Finish with a short list of unresolved questions and one clear next step. Check that the response follows my constraints, avoids repetition, and gives me a usable starting point rather than a general overview.

Work within [change_constraints]. Use the information I supply as your factual basis. Do not invent facts, quotations, source details, or decisions; clearly label any hypothetical examples.
